scenario.title: 跟朋友看棒球、聊比賽
scenario.context: 看球賽時一直在說「期待」：很期待看這場比賽、我一直很想去看職棒。英文的 look forward to 看起來是 to + 原形，其實 to 是介系詞，後面要接 V-ing，這是台灣人（甚至很多老師）最常搞錯的地方之一。

lines.speaker: Ryan
lines.en: I've been looking forward to seeing a CPBL game for months!
lines.zh: 我好幾個月前就很期待看中職比賽了！

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: You picked a good one. The Hawks are the underdogs, but they've been on fire lately.
lines.zh: 你挑了一場好比賽。雄鷹是弱勢的一方，但他們最近很火熱。

lines.speaker: Ryan
lines.en: What's with all the drums and cheerleaders?
lines.zh: 那些鼓和啦啦隊是怎麼回事？

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: When it comes to cheering, Taiwan goes all out. Every player has their own song.
lines.zh: 講到加油，台灣是傾盡全力的，每個球員都有自己的應援曲。

lines.speaker: Ryan
lines.en: I'm not used to hearing so much noise at a baseball game. I love it!
lines.zh: 我不習慣在棒球場聽到這麼吵的聲音。我好愛！

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Watch this guy. He's so clutch. He always hits when it matters.
lines.zh: 看這個人，他超有關鍵時刻的能力，總在最重要的時候擊出安打。

lines.speaker: Ryan
lines.en: Home run! Is he the GOAT or what?
lines.zh: 全壘打！他是不是史上最強？

lines.speaker: Ryan
lines.en: What a game! I can't believe the other team's pitcher choked in the ninth.
lines.zh: 好精彩的比賽！真不敢相信對方投手在第九局失常。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: He must have been nervous. Everyone was screaming.
lines.zh: 他一定很緊張，大家都在尖叫。

lines.speaker: Ryan
lines.en: I'm really into Taiwanese baseball now. I'm committed to learning all the cheer songs.
lines.zh: 我現在超迷台灣棒球。我決心要學會所有應援曲。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Ha! I object to singing the cheer songs in the office, though.
lines.zh: 哈！不過我反對在辦公室唱應援曲。

lines.speaker: Ryan
lines.en: No promises. I look forward to annoying you with them.
lines.zh: 不保證。我很期待用它們來煩你。

patterns.en: I'm looking forward to the playoffs.

chinglish.wrong: I'm looking forward to see the game.
chinglish.right: I'm looking forward to seeing the game.
chinglish.why: look forward to 的 to 是介系詞，後面接 V-ing。這是非常常見的錯誤。
複習第 35 單元：加油不是 fighting。

chinglish.wrong: When it comes to cheer, Taiwan is number one.
chinglish.right: When it comes to cheering, Taiwan is the best.
chinglish.why: when it comes to 的 to 也是介系詞，接 V-ing 或名詞。

chinglish.wrong: The pitcher is very clutch in key moment.
chinglish.why: clutch 本身就是「關鍵時刻表現好」，不用再加 in key moment。

grammar.title: to 當介系詞：look forward to + V-ing
grammar.oneLiner: 有些片語裡的 to 是介系詞，不是不定詞的 to，所以後面接名詞或 V-ing。
whenToUse: look forward to + V-ing：期待。I look forward to hearing from you.
be used to / get used to + V-ing（第 58 單元）。
when it comes to + V-ing / 名詞：說到…
be committed / dedicated to + V-ing：致力於。
in addition to + V-ing：除了…之外。
判斷方法：在 to 後面放一個名詞試試看，如果可以（look forward to the game），那 to 就是介系詞，動詞要用 V-ing。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 台灣人學英文時最早學到的規則之一就是「to 後面接原形」，這個規則太根深蒂固，所以遇到 look forward to 時很自然就接原形。其實 to 有兩種身分：不定詞（want to go）和介系詞（go to school）。當 to 是介系詞時，後面的動詞要變成動名詞。英文 email 最常見的結尾 I look forward to hearing from you，很多人都寫錯。

examples.correct: I look forward to hearing from you.
examples.incorrect: I look forward to hear from you.

examples.correct: When it comes to cooking, my dad is the expert.
I object to working on weekends.
I'm looking forward to the game.
examples.note: to 後面接名詞，證明它是介系詞。

quiz.question: I'm looking forward to ___ you next week.
When it comes to ___ (choose) a team, I always pick the underdog.
Which is correct for an email ending?
options: I look forward to hear from you.
I look forward to hearing from you.
I look forward hearing from you.
quiz.explanation: I look forward to hearing from you。

quiz.question: Our company is committed to ___ more sustainable.
Which "to" is a preposition?
options: I'm used to waking up early.
quiz.explanation: be used to 的 to 是介系詞。

slang.meaning: 處於劣勢的一方、不被看好的隊伍
slang.usage: 被預期會輸的隊伍或人，也用在商業、選舉等。

risk.note: 常見用語，常帶支持意味。

examples.en: I always root for the underdog.
examples.zh: 我總是支持不被看好的一方。

examples.en: The small startup was the underdog, but it won the contract.
examples.zh: 那家小新創不被看好，但拿下了合約。

slang.usage: 形容在壓力最大的時候發揮的人或表現：a clutch hit / He's so clutch.

risk.note: 運動和遊戲用語，也可以開玩笑用在生活中。

examples.en: That was a clutch shot in the last second!
examples.zh: 最後一秒那球太關鍵了！

examples.en: You brought an umbrella? So clutch.

slang.usage: 在壓力下表現失常。choke under pressure。

risk.note: 說別人 choked 帶批評，當事人聽了會難受。

examples.en: He choked in the final and missed an easy shot.
examples.zh: 他在決賽失常，錯過一個很簡單的球。

examples.en: I always choke during job interviews.

slang.meaning: 史上最強（Greatest Of All Time）
slang.usage: 唸成 goat（山羊）。形容某領域的頂尖人物，也常開玩笑用在朋友身上。

risk.note: 年輕人和運動迷常用；有時用山羊表情符號代替。

examples.en: Some people say Messi is the GOAT.
examples.zh: 有些人說梅西是史上最強。

examples.en: You made breakfast for everyone? You're the GOAT.
examples.zh: 你幫大家做早餐？你是神。

review.question: (Formal) We ___ that the game has been postponed.
review.explanation: 複習第 85 單元：正式語域。

review.question: The coach insisted that every player ___ on time.
review.explanation: 複習第 84 單元：insist that + 原形。

review.question: Fans ___ (wear) team jerseys got a discount.
review.explanation: 複習第 82 單元：減化關係子句。

review.question: That guy behind us was ___ shouting at the umpire!
review.explanation: 複習第 78 單元：always + 進行式抱怨。

review.question: If he hadn't dropped the ball, they ___.
Which is the softest comment?

review.explanation: 複習第 54 單元：軟化語氣。

options: I'm agree it was a great game.
I agree it was a great game.

options: I look forward to meet you.
